The first release of **Kaiwa** (会話, *conversation*): a voice tutor you talk to, which remembers what you learned between lessons.

### Download

| Your computer | File |
| --- | --- |
| Windows 10 / 11 | `Kaiwa-v1.0.0-windows-x64.zip` |
| Mac with Apple silicon (M1 and later) | `Kaiwa-v1.0.0-macos-arm64.tar.gz` |
| Mac with an Intel processor | `Kaiwa-v1.0.0-macos-x64.tar.gz` |
| Linux | `Kaiwa-v1.0.0-linux-x64.tar.gz` |
| Linux on ARM | `Kaiwa-v1.0.0-linux-arm64.tar.gz` |

Unpack it and run **Kaiwa**. Your browser opens the app (use Chrome or Edge). The first time, Kaiwa asks for your [OpenAI API key](https://platform.openai.com/api-keys). It's saved on your computer only, and usage is billed to your own OpenAI account.

The builds are not code-signed yet:
- **Windows:** if SmartScreen says *"Windows protected your PC"*, click **More info → Run anyway**.
- **macOS:** right-click **Kaiwa → Open** the first time.

The [README](https://github.com/jeremysaqr/kaiwa#download-and-run) has full instructions.

### What's in it

- Live voice tutoring over WebRTC with the OpenAI Realtime API
- German (tutor Franz) and Japanese (romaji-only), from Absolute Beginner up
- Lessons: hotel front desk, numbers, time and money, restaurant, train station, vocabulary builder, and Word Drill for words you have already saved
- Memory between lessons: vocabulary, weaknesses and an AI-assessed level, stored as plain JSON in a folder you choose
- Several users and languages on one computer
- Add your own lessons by dropping a `lesson.json` into the `Lessons` folder

`SHA256SUMS.txt` lists a checksum for each download.
